clue.text: Not right when there's sauce for Cockney to go after sandwiches

indicators.note: something that sandwiches another holds it in the middle, so the pursuit word wraps around the sauce
a Cockney speaker famously drops the H at the start of words, so the leading H goes

parts.note: to go after something is to hunt it
jus is a thin gravy or sauce, from the French

explanation.surface: A Cockney diner complains about the sauce served after the sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Cockney' drops the H of HUNT, leaving UNT, which 'sandwiches' JUS. Cockneys are working-class Londoners whose accent drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unjust is unfair, not morally right or fair in its treatment of people.

clue.text: Heading north, go round quite posh Scottish town

indicators.note: in a down entry heading north means the letters run upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: to loop is to go round
all, as in all alone, means quite or completely
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Travelling north, someone tours a rather smart Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ullapool is a fishing port in the Scottish Highlands, on Loch Broom.

clue.text: Very full of cracks, is jet ok to fly?

indicators.note: to fly here means the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cracked jet is safe to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks' looks like structural damage but means jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracks are wisecracks, so the most jokey is the most full of quips.

clue.text: Racing employee across lake, go direct

parts.note: a go is an attempt, a stab

indicators.note: across means the guiding word spans the water letter, sitting on both sides of it

parts.note: to direct is to lead
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A racing worker is told to cross a lake and go straight.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable lad looks after racehorses at a training yard.

clue.text: Flyer found in grate, next to something black

indicators.note: next to says the grating word sits beside the dark word, coming after it here

parts.note: the night is black, dark
to grate on someone is to jar, to irritate

explanation.surface: Something that flew in is found in the fireplace grate beside the black soot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grate' looks like a fireplace noun but is the verb meaning irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal bird, so a creature that flies.

clue.text: Too keen on profit, barristers generally admitted

indicators.note: admitted means the lawyers are let in between the other two words

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
gain is profit
barristers as a body are the Bar

explanation.surface: Lawyers are let in for being too greedy for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Into the bargain means in addition, as well, which is what too means.

clue.text: Capital hotel: what every pop star wants?

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a pop star wants a number one hit, A NO 1, with the 1 as I

explanation.surface: A capital hotel is the dream of every pop star.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam.

clue.text: Jack and I getting sticks out as shield, united in selfdefence

indicators.note: as shield means the protruding word surrounds and guards the other letters

parts.note: to jut is to stick out, so juts
J is the card abbreviation for jack
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football team names

explanation.surface: Jack and I hold sticks up as shields, united in defending ourselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Ju-jitsu is a Japanese martial art of unarmed combat used for defence.

clue.text: For which very long-term use results ultimately in wear and tear, say

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of each of the six words before it

explanation.surface: Wear and tear is what long-term use eventually produces.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as machinery ageing, but 'wear' and 'tear' are an example of two words that chime.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear and tear is an example of a pair of words that end with the same sound.

clue.text: Cheers a tallish monk in, wildly

indicators.note: wildly signals the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tall monk joins in the cheering with great excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is informal thanks, and this phrase is an emphatic expression of gratitude.

clue.text: Offer made by barman in dramshop eagerly?

definitions.text: Offer made by barman in dramshop
definitions.meaning: a barman might offer a customer something '...' of spirits
to do it at once, eagerly

explanation.surface: A barman in a bar keenly proposes a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes acting immediately and willingly, without any hesitation.

clue.text: Disappointing outcome that must hold little girl back

indicators.note: back tells you the whole assembled string is read in reverse
to hold something is to contain it, so the pointer word goes around the girl

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word for that
Jo is a short girl's name, as in Little Women

explanation.surface: An unhappy result because someone had to hold a little girl back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the whole of YOJON, not only the girl's name as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting no joy is a colloquial way of saying an effort failed to succeed.

clue.text: Traveller left in vessel — set out early

indicators.note: in places the salesman and the left letter within the cooking vessel

parts.note: a pan is a vessel for cooking
a rep, or commercial traveller, is a travelling salesman

explanation.surface: A traveller left something in a pot before setting out early in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' reads as departing but means arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To preplan is to arrange or organise matters in advance, beforehand.

clue.text: National symbol, not that large, wrapped in note

parts.note: the opposite of that is this

indicators.note: wrapped in puts the size letter inside the musical note

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A national emblem, not a big one, comes gift-wrapped with a note.
explanation.definitionFit: The thistle is the floral emblem of Scotland.

clue.text: Method of counting back only partially useful at court

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
only partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A way of keeping score that is only somewhat helpful in a law court or on a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Octal is the base-eight number system, a way of counting in eights.

clue.text: Be specific about sabbatical?

definitions.meaning: to spell something out is to explain it explicitly and in detail
read as a noun phrase, a ... is a period of time away, as a sabbatical is

explanation.surface: Someone asks for details about a career break.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means explain clearly; the cryptic noun reading means a stint away from work.

clue.text: Trots out to lunch?

parts.note: Trots are Trotskyists, far-left activists, and someone out to lunch is crazy, so mad leftists

explanation.surface: Someone trots off for a lunch break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trots' looks like a verb of jogging but is the noun for Trotskyists; 'out to lunch' is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a derisive British label for extreme socialist politicians, mocked as crazed.

clue.text: Work your English electrical engineer secures after a month

indicators.note: after puts the remaining letters behind the calendar abbreviation

parts.note: Jan is short for January

indicators.note: secures means the engineer letters hold the possessive within them

parts.note: EE is short for electrical engineer
yr is the written abbreviation of your

explanation.surface: An English electrician gets your work done a month later.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Eyre is Charlotte Bronte's novel, a literary work.

clue.text: World of Don, Adam, Erica, somehow not close to sister

indicators.note: somehow says the names' letters are put together in some new way
not removes the chosen letter from the second name
close to picks out the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A world involving Don, Adam and Erica, but not close to a sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not close to sister' removes R, the end of sister, from ERICA; the anagram signal then rearranges ADAM plus EICA. A don is a university lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the scholarly environment of universities, where dons teach and research.

clue.text: Climbing holiday at end of term for ancient art master?

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means the letters run upward, so read in reverse
at end of puts the break word behind the naming word

parts.note: a term is a word or name
a vac is a university vacation, a holiday

explanation.surface: A climbing holiday at the end of term suits an ancient art master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' looks like the school period that precedes holidays, but means a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehistoric people painted on cave walls, as at Lascaux, so a cave dweller was an early artist.

clue.text: City jobs bank has periodically cut

indicators.note: cutting at regular intervals leaves every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Jobs at a city bank have been cut from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major port city in Japan.

clue.text: Eggs sent up: not exactly party food

indicators.note: in a down entry sent up means the letters are read upward, reversed

parts.note: ova are eggs
ca, circa, means about, not exactly
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Eggs were sent up to a party, though not exactly party food.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is a fruit eaten as food, often in salads or dips.

clue.text: Judge comes across cases familiar to Scandinavians?

indicators.note: cases means the crossing word encloses the legal letter as a container

parts.note: to ford a river is to come across it, so fords

explanation.surface: A judge comes across legal cases familiar to Scandinavians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like legal matters but is a containment signal. The definition is elliptical: (things) familiar to Scandinavians.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway's coast is cut by long sea inlets, a feature well known to Nordic people.

clue.text: Old satirist, easily bribed, going to jail briefly

indicators.note: briefly means the slang word for prison is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: jug is slang for jail
venal means corruptible, open to bribery

explanation.surface: An old satirist, open to bribes, ends up briefly in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenal was a Roman poet famous for his Satires.

clue.text: Link we're to follow? There's no time

indicators.note: there's no means the time letter is removed

parts.note: if we're to follow, it is next us, us next

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a link to follow, but there is no time.
explanation.definitionFit: A nexus is a connection or series of connections linking things.

clue.text: Feel being outside on vacation usually means stay at campsite

indicators.note: being outside means the feeling word goes around the shortened adverb

parts.note: to grope is to feel about with the hands

indicators.note: vacated, the word is emptied of its inside, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Feeling the outdoors on holiday usually means staying at a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' leaves UY, the ends of usually. 'stay' is a noun: a rope or wire that supports something.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy rope is a tensioned line anchoring a tent, a kind of stay or support.

clue.text: Rock group backed number selected to play new recording?

parts.note: REM is an American rock band

indicators.note: backed tells you the team number is read backwards

parts.note: a team of eleven, XI, is the number selected to play cricket or football

explanation.surface: A rock band supported a number chosen to play on a new record.
explanation.definitionFit: A remix is a fresh version of a recorded track with its elements rebalanced.

clue.text: Schedule one can track after time

indicators.note: after places the railway abbreviation behind the period of time

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a can is a tin
an era is a period of time
RY is short for railway, a track

explanation.surface: One timetable can follow a set route after a certain time.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerary is a planned route or programme for a journey.

clue.text: American can celebrate with an encore

parts.note: to sing is to celebrate in song
an encore is a repeat performance, so the singing comes again

explanation.surface: Americans can celebrate and then sing again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is US slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Sing Sing is a famous maximum-security prison in New York State; can is US slang for jail.

clue.text: British actor recalled ladies inside hotel, not outside

indicators.note: inside places the reversed toilet word within the trimmed hotel
not outside keeps only the inner letters, dropping the first and last
recalled here means brought back, the word read backwards

parts.note: the ladies is a toilet, a loo

explanation.surface: An actor remembers the ladies' room in a hotel, not outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladies' is British slang for a women's toilet, the loo. Peter O'Toole was born in Ireland or England by differing accounts and worked as a British actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter O'Toole was the stage and screen star of Lawrence of Arabia.
